Detail: Detect the drop. Hold state. Pick up at the exact point it stopped. Clear spoken status. No looping 'no service'.
Keep glasses working while the host phone is in use. Or let glasses read on-phone content straight off: notes, documents.
Reliable non-voice wake: button, gesture, tap. Discreet whisper mode. Longer listening window so questions are fully heard.
Prompt on start: 'continue your last conversation or start new?' Remember recent context across a session.
Directional microphones. Bone conduction. Cupped-hand or whisper pickup. Target restaurants, crowds, church.
Cut the power cost of always-on. Hands-free continuous AI for chores and navigation without the battery hit.

Do this: Opt-in face enrollment and person locating
Detail: User-controlled enrollment of known faces to names. Privacy preserving. Plus 'where is she relative to me?' spatial locating.
Read in full by default. Confirm before summarizing. Flag any condensing so users know something was left out.
Higher-fidelity pipelines for money, rows of numbers, handwriting, color and garment identification. Or auto-handoff to a specialist tool.
Guided setup for online buyers at in-store quality. Live human help. Video onboarding. Longer return window. Equip facilitators.
Cellular or hotspot fallback. Frictionless, safe venue-network switching. Cut the tie to one home Wi-Fi.
Wider field or multi-frame stitching. Proactive off-frame callouts: 'table to your right.' Prevent collisions.
Make the glasses beep. Home in by sound. Last-seen address alone leaves users searching.
Spoken framing and centering guidance while taking photos. Confirm the subject is captured. P002 didn't know this was possible.
Multiple frame widths and a lighter build. Nose pads as standard. Treat fit as an accessibility requirement, since a device that slides off gets left at home.

Prescription options at purchase without gating on a stable script. Near and far correction in one lens, or a reading mode that survives a second pair. Optional untinted lenses for users with low residual vision.

Do this: Ship an activation and utilisation programme
Detail: Owners do not know what they own. Short task-based prompts, a monthly try this, and a facilitator kit. The single cheapest lever on the whole list.

Do this: Speak the framing coaching out loud
Detail: Adopt the guided-capture pattern already shipping on one device. Move closer, turn to the light, stay still, got it. Same for photos before they are sent.

Do this: Cut live AI latency and hold the line
Detail: Treat lag as a release blocker. Publish a latency budget. Do not regress a working continuous mode in an update.

Do this: Run reading and scene recognition on device
Detail: No cloud round trip for the two features that need no world knowledge. Keeps them alive off the grid and out of the venue-network trap.

Do this: Give the user a scope and detail dial
Detail: In my hand only. Short version. Skip the background. Pointing already works as a scope cue, so make it explicit and reliable.

Do this: Teach the reader what numbers mean
Detail: Context-aware numerals. Appliance display, price, dose, temperature, phone number. Say what kind of number it is, or say it cannot tell.
Detect columns, panels and item-plus-description pairs. Read in reading order. Say so when the layout defeats it rather than mismatching silently.
Speaker enrolment so bystanders do not cancel a reply. Reuse the noise handling already proven in video capture.
Infer intent from a partial command. Ask one clarifying question instead of half-acting. Confirm the listening state without depending on a beep the user may miss.
Wake and command in the user's first language. Ship setup and training material in that language. Keep translation output out of the way of the live speaker.

Do this: Make failure recovery safe and hands-off
Detail: Announce a dropped connection, retry automatically, and never require fiddling. Add a do not disturb me now state for exercise, stairs, and street.

Do this: Give the answer a confidence signal
Detail: Say how sure it is. Flag anything the user cannot check. Trust ratings sit at 4 to 5 with almost no verification behind them, which is a risk, not a result.

Do this: Make person description a user setting
Detail: Let the wearer choose what they receive: ethnicity, gender and age estimates, expression, or appearance only. Best guess with the reason attached, stated as a guess.

Do this: Close the loop from reading to acting
Detail: If it can read a control, let it help operate it. Hand off to the screen reader or drive the tap.
One-ear output, whisper volume, and a quick physical volume control the user can find without the app.
No more than three functions per control. Split settings and diagnostics onto a second control. Offer a left or right touchpad.
Volume control on case alerts, or a silent mode. Nobody should be unable to open the case in a library.
Mirror mode, or a way to check hair, makeup and outfit without a second person. Ask how do I look and get a straight answer.
Third-party assistants and apps, all major messaging platforms, maps and points-of-interest search. On niche hardware, publish a continuity commitment so a shutdown does not brick the device.
Position the device as the option when nobody is around, and make that case explicit. Otherwise the helper wins by default and the device never gets used.
Doneness, cleanliness, fullness, flame on or off. Where safety is involved, give a reading plus a limit statement rather than refusing outright.
Tell me when you see gate 14. Tell me when we reach the cereal aisle. Standing alerts rather than repeated scene scans.
Sports, concerts, conferences. Leaderboards, crowd scenes, live commentary gaps. Named unprompted as the highest-value future use.

Do this: Say when it cannot see, never invent
Detail: Refuse rather than fabricate on a partial or lost frame. Hold the captured image and answer follow-ups from it, or say the frame is gone. A single fabrication costs the whole use case.

Do this: Publish time to first correct read
Detail: One attempt, not three. Treat retries as the core metric, since patience is what users actually spend and paid work has none to spare.
Distinct start and stop tones, a spoken confirmation on request, and a running indicator. Never let a clip fail silently.

Do this: Coach the frame, then confirm the shot
Detail: Speak the framing guidance out loud before capture. Confirm what landed in the shot afterwards. The pattern already ships on one device in the study.

Do this: Name clips so they can be found by ear
Detail: Timestamp plus a one-line description of the content. Optional spoken label at capture. Preserve capture order on import.

Do this: Keep assistive audio out of the take
Detail: Duck or route screen reader speech away from the recording. Creators should not have to choose between hearing their device and using the footage.

Do this: Hand the text off to the phone
Detail: Push captured text to the app with a notification. Re-readable, saveable, searchable, brailleable. Let the user jump to a section by name.

Do this: Ground location answers in the actual location
Detail: Use the device position, not the metro area or the airport, for weather, transit and nearby places. Say which position it used.

Do this: Make it audible on a loud street
Detail: Directional or bone conduction output tuned for noise, a boost mode, and an optional single earbud handoff. Users are already cupping a hand around one ear.
Sensor and low light performance at phone parity. Remote volunteers currently ask people to put the glasses away and use the phone.

Do this: Pair to two devices at once
Detail: Phone and tablet or computer together, with a spoken switch. Table stakes on a mid-range headset.

Do this: Design for print that was never designed for reading
Detail: Low contrast mode, glare and lamination handling, text inside marketing images, and a straight answer when the page defeats it. Publish guidance to brands, since sighted customers are failing on the same pages.

Do this: Ship opt-in face enrollment from the contact list
Detail: Name only, from photos the user already has, plus a direction and rough distance. Four participants have now asked unprompted. Scope it narrowly and privacy review gets easier.
Detect the installed partner app and offer the link in one step from either side. Capability sitting unused for eighteen months is capability that was never shipped.
Say what went wrong and what would fix it: move closer, more light, turn the item. Silence gets read as personal failure and ends in lower use.

Do this: Give an answer the user can check alone
Detail: Confidence level, source, and a second look on request. For anyone without a sighted person on hand, an unverifiable answer is the same as no answer.

Do this: Never agree to please on a safety question
Detail: Doneness, cleanliness, flame, spoilage. Give a reading with its limits, or decline plainly. Suspected flattery is why the whole kitchen use case is off.

Do this: Defend the accommodation case in public
Detail: Clear wearer-facing indicator state, a published accessibility position for venues, and support for users challenged over wearing them. Bans and hostility land on blind wearers first.

Do this: Design for partial sight, not only for blindness
Detail: Contrast, magnification handoff, and language that does not assume no vision. Half the study now has usable residual sight and gets read as having none.

Do this: Separate what it sees from what it sells
Detail: State plainly that camera and conversation content is not used for ad targeting, or let users switch it off. This is the only privacy objection in the study that changed behaviour.
Plates, house numbers, faces, documents. Warn before posting, offer automatic blurring. Bystander protection is what the wearer actually asks for.
No truncation to the phone. Long message, long read, with a stop command and a resume point.
Too small, too dark, glare, upside down, out of frame. Report the same way on every device and every failure.
Residual sight fades through the day. Let the device lean in later, and stop assuming a fixed level of vision.

Do this: Drive the screens in the world, or admit the gap
Detail: Bridge to kiosk and payment terminals, or publish the accessibility position and route the user to a person. This is the barrier one participant ranks above every device defect.

Do this: Never answer from a stale frame
Detail: Timestamp the capture. Refuse rather than reuse. Say the frame is gone and take another.

Do this: Separate policy refusals from capture failures
Detail: Say plainly that the answer is withheld and why. A refusal that sounds like a failure teaches the user the device is broken.

Do this: Make enrollment consent legible to the enrolled
Detail: On-device storage, a visible list, a way for the enrolled person to see and delete their entry. The block is not the wearer's privacy, it is the family's.

Do this: Let a capture leave by voice
Detail: Send to a saved contact, email or drive with one spoken command. Never answer a capture request with steps for an app the user cannot see.
Multi-angle capture, cylindrical unwrapping, or say plainly that the shape is defeating it and ask for a turn.
Digital zoom on request, or a magnification handoff. For residual sight, enlarging is the function, not describing.
A setting that strips pleasantries, affirmations and conversational framing. Answer, then stop.
A replaceable cell or a serviceable arm. Publish an expected capacity curve. A sealed battery turns an accessibility device into a consumable.
Bind configuration to the account, not the hardware. Owning a spare should cost nothing.

Do this: Cut time to first useful answer
Detail: Keep the link warm, pre-stage the volunteer call, and report the connection state out loud. The clock starts when the user decides, not when the call lands.
Expected wait, a paid fallback, and a route that does not depend on a stranger being awake.

Do this: Give the remote helper a usable image
Detail: Higher resolution on a live assist call, a still capture on request, and a zoom control the helper can drive.
One consistent low-confidence behaviour. If it cannot name the product, say so. A wrong brand delivered fluently costs the whole use case.

Do this: Give narration a pause and a gesture
Detail: Tap to pause, tap to resume. Duck automatically when the wearer starts speaking.
A checklist the user sets: hazards, people, shops, signs, scenery. Default to hazards and people.
Match screen reader rates. Blind users read faster than the maximum on offer.

Do this: Answer no with what it does see
Detail: Never a bare negative. No escalator, but there is a corridor ahead and a staircase to your left.
The camera sits where the hazard is. Branches, signs, open cupboards and shelf edges, called early enough to duck.
Charge level and pairing announced on open, or reported by the glasses. Never a colour the wearer cannot see.

Do this: Never refuse on a state the user cannot verify
Detail: If it thinks a call is active, say so and offer to clear it. Phantom states with no escape are worse than plain failures.

Do this: Fix the reputation, not just the bug
Detail: Community demonstrations of corrected failures. A fix nobody hears about does not reopen a retired use case.

Do this: Design for a full day on a face
Detail: Nose pads, weight distribution and pressure testing across hours, not minutes. Fit and pressure are the two hardware causes of reduced use in this study.

Do this: Build for the way blind people move
Detail: Impact-rated frames and lenses, a replaceable arm, and an accidental-damage plan. The device is worn by people who walk into things.

Do this: Guide the turn on a medication bottle
Detail: Detect a partial label, say which way to rotate, confirm when the name is in view. The volunteer script already exists; automate it.
Hold the page, take several frames, assemble one reading, say when the page is fully covered.
On-device processing, a layout-only mode that reports fixtures and suppresses people. The wearer wants to protect bystanders, not to give up the room.
Splash and rain resistance at minimum. Water rules out a whole class of outdoor activity that the device is otherwise suited to.
Detect a refreshing display, capture a stable frame, or say the screen changed mid-read.
Top left, third row, between my fingers, the total at the bottom. Pointing already works as a cue; make the spoken version work too.
Answer in body-relative terms by default. Left, right, ahead, and a distance in steps or feet. Suppress right there, this one and in front of you unless a distance is attached.
Give the user something to check against. A confidence band, a second independent read, a spoken account of what the frame contained, or a one-tap handoff to a human on the same image.

Do this: Treat absence as a low-confidence answer
Detail: Never assert that a thing is not present. Say the frame does not show one, name what was in the frame, and offer another capture.
Hold the session through head movement and bending. On a drop, resume where it stopped instead of resetting.
When a read or colour request would return a scene description, say so first. What colour is this should never answer with the room.
Short burst or video sampling for anything that blinks, alternates or moves. Report the change, the colour and the position.
Foods, garments and objects outside the dominant training distribution. Where confidence is low, describe rather than name.

Do this: A capability changelog users can hear
Detail: Announce what changed on update, in the app and on request. Include what was withdrawn and why.
Keep the same voice and the same audio profile in live mode, and keep ambient hearing intact.
Never offer or begin a call, a message or a mode change that was not asked for. Live mode should require an explicit start.
A single spoken command to hold announcements during media, and a plain path to it in setup.

Do this: Report the selection, not only the screen
Detail: Name which item is highlighted, and support move to the next one as a spoken action.
Coaching the user can follow without sight. Where the fix is impossible, say what the device can do with the frame it already has.
Faster scanning, a discreet mode, and a way to signal to staff that this is an access device rather than surveillance.

Do this: Legibility as a blind person’s device
Detail: Frames that do not read as ordinary eyewear to bystanders, or a visible signal that the wearer is not looking back.

Do this: A recording state the wearer can verify
Detail: Spoken or haptic confirmation of the indicator, so the wearer can answer a challenge without guessing.
A standing watch on colour, make and plate, announced when the car is close, with a direction and a distance.
Report unoccupied seats with position, in pews, buses and waiting rooms.
